title: SAML group-sync race leading to transient admin elevation and incomplete audit events
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: A customer reported a support incident where a subset of users observed either permission denied errors immediately after an SSO login or—conversely—briefly elevated admin UI controls before their roles reverted. Investigation shows a race between SAML group-sync worker retries and the RBAC v2 policy write path. When a group sync for a user is retried after a transient IdP timeout, the local ‘roles.apply’ write can succeed while the audit-log writer for SSO-derived grants is still backoff-retrying; in some cases the audit entry for grant creation is never persisted due to an unhandled error path. Root cause: the group-sync flow had non-atomic apply-and-log semantics. The state machine allowed apply() to return success while async audit flushes were left unobserved; retries could re-apply different role sets and temporarily expose UI controls tied to the first applied role. This also highlighted insufficient idempotency for group->role mappings when duplicate SAML assertions arrived near-simultaneously.

Impact: Intermittent permission-denied failures for users (blocking workflows) and transient over-permissioned UI exposure for others. Missing audit records for those role changes made post-incident forensic analysis incomplete. Affected customers: two enterprise customers using IdP-initiated login with aggressive session lifetimes and one self-managed Private deployment.

Repro steps (internal):
1) Configure SAML group attribute sync with overlapping group mappings (group A -> engineer, group B -> admin). 2) Introduce artificial latency to IdP response (200-400ms) and trigger two near-concurrent SAML assertions for the same user (simulate browser + background refresh). 3) Observe that first assertion hits applyRole(given set) while audit writer experiences transient DB deadlock and retries; second assertion completes and flips role set. 4) UI reads role cache between writes and shows admin controls briefly. 5) Audit entries show only the second change or are missing entirely if audit write failed before retry succeeded.

Proposed fix:
- Make group-sync apply-and-log an atomic operation: change to a two-phase commit within the RBAC service where role assignment is only considered "complete" after the audit write is durably persisted. This will be implemented by adding a transactional wrapper around role write + audit insert or using an audit buffer with synchronous flush for SSO-derived grants.
- Add stronger idempotency keys for SAML assertions (assertion-id + user) so duplicate assertions don't create conflicting transient states.
- Improve backoff/alerting: if audit flush fails the API returns 5xx and the auth flow triggers a retry instead of returning success to the session layer.
- Add a short-lived UI guard: route-level check to re-fetch authoritative roles (or mark UI controls read-only) until role assignment+audit confirmed for the session.

Rollout plan:
- Stage changes in a canary Dedicated pool (canary-2) with synthetic SAML assertion tests in CI. (automation in repo: infra/tests/saml-race). Run smoke tests with customer-specific group mappings.
- Deploy to Hosted API with feature flag rbac_v2_sync_atomic (off by default). Enable for internal tenants and the two impacted customers first.
- Monitor audit log success rates, role flip frequency, and customer error reports for 72h before broad enabling.

Testing and validation:
- New unit tests for transactional apply-and-log semantics.
- End-to-end integration test that replays SAML assertions at various timings asserting no transient admin UI exposure and audit rows present.
- Load test to validate audit write sync does not violate latency SLOs beyond acceptable thresholds; if it does, implement a fast-path cached-audit entry with guaranteed durable background replication.

Backports: Patch required for Private deployments (release patch-2.4.1). Notify on-prem customers and provide migration notes for DB schema change (audit table index for assertion-id). Confluence runbook will be updated.

Notes on incident handling: opened customer incident INC-2026-1031; compensation and support actions coordinated with CSM. Customer-facing root cause statement prepared for approval.
